To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the on-resonance PV ensemble method is applicable to the study of PV in isolated resonance targets and the minimum sample size for quantitative studies of PV in the isolated resonance case is given approximately by the ratio of the resonance strength to the PV strength.

(1) the PV spreading width is a quantity that is well defined for isolated resonances, but that its extraction from experimental data requires a large amount of data, and (2) the PV spreading widths extracted for the 3.8 and 5.4 eV resonances of 209Bi are 2.0(5) and 2.0(+5,-3) eV respectively.
the two-state approximation can be safely used to extract the PV width of the isolated resonance if the target is large enough, the target is not too thin and the target is not in the ground state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and testing of a new method to measure parity violation (PV), which is a very small effect, and to improve the precision of the measurements.
the development of a new technique for measuring the parity-violating (PV) asymmetry in the scattering of polarized neutrons on the target nuclei of a sample.

the development of the theoretical and practical tools required for the quantitative analysis of PV experiments in the isolated resonance region, with the aim of establishing a quantitative link between the PV observables and the fundamental properties of the nuclear wave function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for targets with a single resonance in the energy range of interest, a minimum number of 20 measurements is necessary to extract reliable values for the parity violating width.
the two-state approximation is a good one in the isolated resonance case, but that the quantitative extraction of a spreading width is a difficult task.
the present status of the theory and experimental techniques is such that quantitative studies of nuclear parity non-conservation are now feasible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a reliable quantitative study of PV in the isolated resonance region is only possible for a few nuclei.

the two-state approximation is not sufficient for the quantitative study of PV above neutron threshold, and that the on-resonance approach is required for the reliable determination of the PV spreading width.

, in principle, the PV spreading width is a measurable quantity in the neutron resonance region, provided that the target has a sufficiently large number of independent neutron resonances, and the data are analysed using an appropriate theoretical model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a quantitative measurement of the nuclear PV asymmetry requires a large number of independent measurements.

, in order to extract reliable PV spreading widths, the data must be collected with a target of sufficiently large spin and a neutron energy sufficiently high that the PV spreading width is much less than the target width.
the two-state approximation, which is widely used in the literature, is not applicable in practice for PV experiments in the isolated resonance region.
